_intent: Roles are the stable abstraction. Agents name a role; the role names models. When the model catalogue changes you edit this file only - never the agents.
principles: Reviewing is where model quality pays for itself. Reasoning agents get the best Claude model, and cost is not a consideration there.
Producing, searching and summarising is where money leaks. Those roles get the cheapest model that can actually finish the job.

Cheap is measured, not assumed. See registry/models.json blended cost - Claude Sonnet 5 (3.60) undercuts GPT-5.4 (5.00), GPT-5.5 (10.00) and Gemini 3.5 Flash. Substituting a GPT model for Sonnet 5 can cost MORE.
Fewer tokens beats a cheaper model. Restricting tools, capping turns and demanding conclusions instead of transcripts saves more than any model swap.
Never pick a model that is dominated - worse AND pricier than an alternative. models.json flags these in notes.

review.intent: Correctness, security and architecture review. Judgement work where a missed bug costs more than the tokens.
review.rationale: Opus 5 is the top merit score in the catalogue and the owner prefers Claude reasoning and output. GPT-6 Astra is the only non-Claude fallback rated equal on merit, so it sits last as an availability backstop rather than a cost saving - it costs 2x Opus 5.

deep-reasoning.intent: Planning, architecture design, tricky debugging, ambiguous tradeoffs.
deep-reasoning.rationale: A bad plan is paid for by every downstream agent, so this is the wrong place to economise. GPT-5.6 Sol is the best-value non-Claude fallback at merit 4.5.

implement.intent: Write real code against a clear spec. Needs competence, not brilliance.
implement.rationale: Sonnet 5 leads on merit-per-dollar in the standard tier (merit 4.0 at blended 3.60) and is CHEAPER than the GPT models a naive cost rule would swap it for. If a workplace policy forbids Sonnet by name regardless of price, reorder to Gemini 3.7 Flash first - see docs/routing.md.

bulk-edit.intent: Mechanical, verifiable changes - renames, import fixes, formatting, codemods, boilerplate.
bulk-edit.rationale: The work is checkable by tests or by eye, so model judgement barely matters. MAI-Code-1.1-Flash is code-tuned at the price floor (blended 0.40).

search.intent: Locate code, trace usages, answer where-is questions. Read-only reconnaissance.
search.rationale: Search burns input tokens by the bucket and needs almost no reasoning. Gemini 3.7 Flash is second for its large context when a sweep is genuinely wide.

summarize.intent: Condense logs, diffs, docs, meeting notes, test output into something a human or a premium agent can read.
summarize.rationale: Highest-leverage cheap role in the kit: a summarizer that compresses 50k tokens of logs to 500 before a premium agent reads them saves more than any model swap.

write-prose.intent: Docs, READMEs, commit messages, PR descriptions, changelogs.
write-prose.rationale: Claude Haiku 4.5 is listed third for when Claude-style prose is worth 4.5x the Luna price.

workplace_overrides._note: Applied by scripts/build.ps1 -Profile work. Use this to satisfy an employer policy without forking the agent definitions.

work.description: Employer asks that Anthropic models be reserved for work that needs them. Review and deep-reasoning keep Claude (that IS the need); producer roles move to non-Anthropic models even where Sonnet 5 would be cheaper.

personal.description: No policy constraint - route purely on measured cost and merit. This is the default.
